- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is positive but recent prices are flat or declining, model overestimates upward momentum — reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean by 2–5% when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — apply downward bias of 2–3% to 30d forecast mean.
- When sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust — reduce forecast from 10–15 days onward by 3–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate true decline — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast for next 7 days.
- Model often underestimates true volatility in sentiment-driven corrections — increase forecast variance by 10–15% during sentiment swings > ±0.3.
